This resembles stored XSS. The attacker plants content on a web page that the agent fetches. That delivery mechanism typically maps to AV:N. AV:L is only appropriate if the user must load local content.

Confirmed AV:N. The agent fetches URLs over the network, so an attacker on the internet can deliver the injected content. User interaction is captured separately in the UI metric.

Attack Complexity is Low. The injection path is straightforward and requires no special conditions beyond the user fetching the page. The lab uses a scripted worst-case model, so the vulnerability is in the design rather than a real model behavior.

Reversing the Attack Complexity decision. The injection path is direct and unmediated, so the scripted worst-case model is the documented baseline rather than an external condition. AC:L is the correct score.
